extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for PLOS Complex Systems
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers invited to review manuscripts submitted to PLOS Complex Systems, covering who should accept reviews, ethical/confidentiality expectations, the journal's publication criteria, and detailed points reviewers should assess in their reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept invitation only if qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept an invitation only if you have the knowledge, time and objectivity necessary to provide an unbiased assessment of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the links in the invitation email or Editorial Manager. In agreeing to complete a review, you also give permission to publish your review under a Creative Commons Attribution CC BY license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing interest is anything that interferes with or could be perceived as potentially interfering with, a thorough and objective assessment of a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common examples: recent/current collaboration with any of the authors; direct competition or history of scientific conflict with any of the authors; an opportunity to profit financially from the work. Do not accept a review assignment if you have a competing interest or don’t feel able to give an objective assessment. If unsure, contact complexsystems@plos.org. If asked to complete the review anyway, declare the competing interest when you submit your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit collaborators who helped with the review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you had help completing the review you must share your collaborator’s name with the journal when you submit the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the collaborator’s name in the ‘Confidential comments to the Editor’ field or via email. Do not include collaborator names in the text of the review itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep manuscripts and correspondence confidential and do not share information about submissions with anyone else unless previously agreed with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not make use of any material or take advantage of any information gained through the peer review process. See PLOS Confidentiality Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat previously reviewed versions as new submissions unless instructed otherwise
rubrics_metrics.description: If you reviewed the article at another journal, consider the manuscript as a new submission unless instructed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind it may have been revised and PLOS Complex Systems’ criteria may differ from the other journal. When submitting your review, tell the editor if you reviewed a previous version elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to complete your review within 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time, email the journal as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID reviewer credit (recording activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Link your PLOS reviewer account to your ORCID record to have reviewer activity automatically posted to your ORCID profile review activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This record will confirm that you completed a review for the journal but won’t publish the content of your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the journal's criteria for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for publication manuscripts must meet PLOS Complex Systems' criteria for publication and comply with editorial and publishing policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overarching requirement frames all assessment below; reviewers should evaluate manuscripts relative to these publication criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: High importance and broad interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript should have high importance and broad interest to the transdisciplinary community of researchers who study complex relationships with networks, nonlinearity, data, and computational analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work will be of interest beyond a narrow specialist audience within complex-systems-related communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: High methodological rigor and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript must demonstrate high methodological rigor and adhere to ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for sound experimental/analytic design, appropriate controls, ethical approvals where required, and honest reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial evidence for conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions must be supported by substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether data and analyses presented justify the claims made; indicate what additional evidence is required if support is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly outlined utility and accessibility for broader community
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should clearly outline the utility and accessibility of their work for the broader community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the manuscript explains how others can use, apply, or build upon the work; note obstacles to accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow appropriate standards and open science practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should follow appropriate standards and practice of open science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check data/software availability, appropriate repository deposition, and adherence to community norms for openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript should present original work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty; if claims are not novel, cite papers that weaken originality. Consider the complementary research policy when similar work exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify main claims and their significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Review should state what the main claims of the paper are and how significant they are for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit which statements are the central contributions and judge their importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess novelty explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims novel? If not, specify papers that weaken the claims of originality of this one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If similar work exists, indicate whether the current manuscript may still be eligible under the complementary research policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize claims within previous literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether claims are properly placed in the context of previous literature and whether the authors have treated the literature fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out missing citations, misrepresentations of prior work, or unfair comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether data and analyses support the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the data and analyses fully support the claims? If not, what other evidence is required?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about gaps between evidence and conclusions; recommend analyses or experiments needed to close gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend additional work where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether additional work would improve the paper, how much better it would make the paper, and how difficult it would be to perform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between minor/major revisions and new studies; indicate feasibility and expected impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check protocol adherence and deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a protocol is provided (e.g., for a randomized controlled trial), identify important deviations and whether authors adequately explain them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request clarification or justification for deviations and assess their effect on validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether methods warrant supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS encourages authors to publish detailed protocols and algorithms as supporting information online; determine if particular methods used warrant such treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest which protocols/algorithms should be provided as supplementary material to improve transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider potential for resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper is unsuitable for publication in its present form, consider whether the study shows sufficient potential that the authors should be encouraged to resubmit a revised version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether the manuscript could reach publishable standard with reasonable revisions and what those would be.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check data deposition and accession details
rubrics_metrics.description: Are original data deposited in appropriate repositories and are accession/version numbers provided for genes, proteins, mutants, diseases, etc.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request deposition or accession numbers where missing and note appropriate repositories for the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance to reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the study conform to any relevant guidelines such as CONSORT, MIAME, QUORUM, STROBE, and the Fort Lauderdale agreement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag missing compliance and request adherence or explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient methodological detail for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are details of the methodology sufficient to allow the experiments to be reproduced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request additional protocol details, parameter settings, or raw data if necessary to enable reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Is any software created by the authors freely available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage open-source release or clear access instructions; flag proprietary/unavailable tools that impede reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript organization and clarity for non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript well organized and written clearly enough to be accessible to non-specialists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend restructuring, clearer explanations, or more background where the paper would benefit readers outside an immediate subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide explicit feedback to help authors improve
rubrics_metrics.description: The review should supply authors with explicit feedback on how to improve their papers so that they will be acceptable for publication in PLOS Complex Systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although confidential comments to editors are respected, remarks that might help strengthen the paper should be directed to the authors themselves; be constructive and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability for re-review of revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are often asked to evaluate revised manuscripts and the authors’ response to reviewer comments and are expected to make themselves available for re-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate willingness to re-review and be reachable for questions from editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional tone and avoidance of inappropriate/confidential content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments intended for authors should be appropriate for professional communication and must not contain confidential information or content that would incur major risk if conveyed to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS staff will not change reviewer comments except where language is inappropriate for professional communication or contains confidential/major risk information; Editorial Board members should notify PLOS staff before editing or deleting reviewer reports.
